01 honest.about: All 64 validators honest, on 4 nodes, 200 ms latency. This is the reference run: the confirmed tip runs one slot behind the head, each node holds k = 4 live locks (the dots of the lock panel), and the finalized tip draws a sawtooth 16–24 slots behind: one FG height per 8-slot round, finalized two rounds after its target.

02 partition 50-50.about:
Two halves of 32 validators each (nodes 0,1 | 2,3), cut for slots 48–63, no adversary. Each half confirms its own branch and passes the fast test (32 ≥ n/2), so both halves fast-lock conflicting branches. Neither reaches q = 43, so finality stalls.

At the heal each lock has exactly 32 opponents and moves back to the last common block: every block of the cut is discarded on both sides (hollow). Heads agree at once, and finality resumes within two rounds.

03 partition 75-25.about: Cut 48–63 with 48 validators on one side and 16 on the other. The majority does not notice the cut: it keeps confirming, fast-locking and finalizing. The minority confirms its own blocks and slow-locks them after k = 4 confirmations. At the heal the majority's votes unlock the minority, which reorgs onto the majority chain (depth 3).

04 partition 52-48.about: Cut 48–63 with 33 validators against 31. Only the 33-side passes the fast test (66 ≥ 64). At the heal its locks have 31 opponents (fewer than n/2) and survive, while the 31-side's locks have 33 and move back. The larger side's branch wins and the other side reorgs (depth 7).

05 long cut 50-50.about: As tab 02, but the cut lasts 64 slots (48–111). Each node discards 28–35 confirmed blocks, and finality stalls for 8 rounds and then resumes. Healing is still immediate: no lock survives the heal.

06 messy heal.about: A 50/50 cut for slots 48–63 whose held messages are released at random times up to 12 s (2 slots) after the heal, instead of all at once. Healing is measured against the moment the last message lands (effective GST). Across 320 seeded runs, heads and confirmed tips always agreed within about three slots, far inside the spec's 2L + G bound.

07 one-slot glitch at a round start.about: A one-slot 50/50 cut at slot 48, the first slot of round 6. The confirmation update of slot 48 gets only 32 votes before the support cutoff on every node. The FG reads its source only from that update, so nobody attests in round 6 and the round is lost for finality: the step expected at slot 50 comes at 58. The same cut at slot 49 costs one slot.

08 half asleep.about: Nodes 2 and 3 (32 validators) are asleep for slots 48–63 (purple band). The awake half keeps confirming and slow-locks, but 32 is less than q = 43, so finality stalls. On waking, the sleepers restart, keep their locks (expired by then) and rejoin within a slot. Finality resumes a round later.

09 adversary: silent.about:
From this tab on, 21 of 64 validators (32.8%) are faulty and run by one adversary. The 43 honest validators sit on 4 nodes (11/11/10/11). Here the adversary is silent: it never votes, proposes or attests, so its proposer slots stay empty.

The 43 honest validators are exactly the quorum q = 43, so finality needs every one of them, and gets it.

10 adversary: equivocation.about:
Every slot, every faulty validator votes two conflicting heads, one to each half of the network. At its proposer slots the adversary proposes two blocks, one per half (X in the tree).

Honest nodes relay everything, including the second vote, so both copies reach everyone within Δ. The equivocators are detected and excluded from confirmations and unlocking, and nothing breaks.

11 adversary: two-faced across a cut.about:
A 50/50 cut for slots 48–63 (nodes 0,1 | 2,3). During the cut the adversary acts honestly on both sides at once: votes, blocks and attestations to each side. Side A plus the adversary reaches q and finalizes on its own (allowed before GST). After the heal it releases blocks it kept back during the cut.

Finality resumes 10 slots after the heal. Across 2,304 seeded runs of this kind, nothing broke after GST.

12 ATTACK fin_hide.about:
The attack. Synchrony throughout: every honest message and every relay arrives within 200 ms, there is one clock, and everything is relayed. The adversary (21/64) proposes slots 33 and 34; slot 34 is the first slot after the round's action time.

Slot 33. Its block B (X) reaches nodes 0 and 3 just before their vote (22 honest votes; nodes 1 and 2 vote W). 10 faulty votes for B arrive early everywhere, which makes exactly 32 = n/2 early votes. 11 faulty validators keep their slot-33 votes back.

Slot 34. Three adversary blocks:

  • FB extends B and carries the round's finality pairs. Only nodes 0–2 get it, 100 ms before their vote.
  • Q forks off at slot 17, below the checkpoint that FB finalizes, and carries the 11 held-back votes.
  • Z is a sibling of B.

Node 3 gets Q and Z 1 ms before its vote. Nodes 0–2 get Q by relay only after FB, so they refuse it: it does not extend their new finalized block, and its votes never reach their available chain.

Node 3 counts 64 voters, so B (32) is not a majority and node 3 votes Z, as does the adversary. Nodes 0–2 count 53 voters: B is confirmed and fast-locked, and is their confirmed tip in slot 34. In slot 35, Z's 32 votes are n/2 opponents, the locks move back, and B is orphaned (hollow).
zooms: s34: FB, Q, Z — nodes 0–2 confirm B
s35: locks move back, B orphaned

13 ATTACK fin_hide, > n/2.about:
The same attack with the strict fast test (> n/2, not the spec). Nodes 0–2 write no lock on B, but 32 of 53 voters is still a strict majority, so they confirm B. The adversary sends its Z votes only to the slot-35 proposer, just before it proposes. Nodes 0–2 keep B as their confirmed tip for 3–4.5 s, then their head moves and B is orphaned.

So > n/2 protects fast locks but not the confirmed tip: 74 of 74 attacked seeds when the Z votes land just before the freeze (shown for 1.5 s), 48 of 74 with this proposer-only variant (shown for 3–4.5 s).

14 ATTACK fin_hide + fix.about: The same attack with the proposed fix (not the spec): the available chain takes the votes of a block even when the FG refuses it. Nodes 0–2 then count the 11 held-back votes too, so B has 32 of 64 voters everywhere and nobody confirms it. Nothing is orphaned. Tab 17 shows the other fix, forwarding the carried votes, which the live spec adopted. Either fix closes every variant, with either threshold (0 of 74 attacked seeds), and 200 random runs stay clean.

15 ATTACK fin_hide_seq, no equivocation.about:
The attack without equivocation. Synchrony throughout (200 ms relay). The adversary (21/64) proposes slots 42, 43 and 44, one block each, and signs nothing conflicting.

  • Slot 42: FB, on the honest head W, carries the round's attestations. The adversary keeps it back.
  • Slot 43: B, on W, reaches nodes 0–2 just before their vote: 32 honest votes, exactly n/2. Node 3 votes W. The 21 faulty validators keep their votes (all for W) back.
  • Slot 44: Q forks below slot 26, the block that FB finalizes, and carries the 21 hidden votes. Q reaches node 3 1 ms before its vote; FB reaches nodes 0–2 100 ms before theirs.

Node 3 accepts Q and counts 64 voters: B is not a majority, so it votes W. Nodes 0–2 have just finalized slot 26, so they refuse Q and count 43 voters. At t44+2Δ they confirm B (2·32 > 43) and fast-lock it (2·32 ≥ 64).

From slot 45 the faulty validators vote W. Nodes 0–2 (locked on B, 32 votes) and node 3 with the faulty validators (11 + 21 = 32) tie, so B never regains a majority. The lock expires at t48+Δ and B is orphaned: nodes 0–2 show B as confirmed for 22.5 s. The tie also orphans the honest blocks of slots 47 and 48.
zooms: s44: FB and Q; B confirmed

16 ATTACK fin_hide_seq, first-seen gossi.about: The run of tab 15 under Ethereum's gossip rule: a node ignores a proposer's second block for a slot and relays only the first copy of each vote. This attack has one block per slot and one vote per validator, so the rule changes nothing: nodes 0–2 show B as confirmed for 22.5 s, as in tab 15. The attack with equivocation (tab 12) fails under this rule.

17 ATTACK fin_hide_seq + vote forwarding.about:
The run of tab 15 with the rule of the live Goldilocks spec (Nov 2026, ethlabs-org/eth-consensus-lean): an honest node forwards the votes it admits from an accepted block as messages of their own, whether or not other nodes accept that block (--relay-carried).

Node 3 accepts Q at t44+Δ−1 ms and forwards the 21 hidden votes. They reach nodes 0–2 before their update at t44+2Δ, so every node counts 64 voters, B (32) is not a majority anywhere, and nobody confirms it. No honest block is orphaned.

The timing is tight by design: an honest node votes by t44+Δ, the update runs at t44+2Δ, and forwarding takes less than Δ. Every vote that changed an honest vote reaches every node before its update.

18 ATTACK fin_hide_df, slow attestations.about:
The attack when attestations are slower than blocks: ΔF = 8Δ = 12 s (the spec only asks ΔF ≥ Δ). The adversary delays every honest attestation of the round as far as ΔF allows and keeps its own, so no honest proposer can finalize before then.

FB therefore no longer has to sit just before B. Here it is the adversary's block of slot 42, built late on the newest block older than slot 42 and carrying every honest attestation; slot 43 is an honest block. B is slot 44 and Q slot 45, as in tab 15.

Nodes 0–2 finalize slot 28 through FB, refuse Q, confirm and lock B, and show it for 22.5 s before it is orphaned. The attack needs B and Q consecutive plus one earlier adversary slot in the round, instead of three consecutive slots: with ΔF = 8Δ about 11% of rounds qualify, against 4% when ΔF = Δ.

19 adversary: late justification, contes.about:
A frontier contest, built on purpose. Nodes 0–1 and 2–3 are cut apart for slots 50–57, over an FG action time, so each side enters height 7 at its own block. The faulty validators side with each half and also justify side A's entry inside a block X_A that the adversary keeps (slot 62). After the heal everyone follows side B; side A and the faulty validators time out at height 7.

At slot 68 the adversary reveals X_A: every node now holds a justification at height 7 on a branch that its height-8 blocks do not extend, a contest, for 6 slots (68–73). No equivocation is needed.

The contest is harmless here. The spec's rule and the Lean model's (which ignores contests) give the same outcome, and the one round of finality lost comes from the split targets: the same run without the reveal loses it too.

20 outage of 3 slots, B kept.about:
How long an asynchronous period a fast confirmation survives. The honest block B of slot 44 is confirmed and fast-locked everywhere at t45+2Δ. Then every node is cut off from every other for 3 slots, [t47+Δ, t50+Δ), while the adversary votes for C, a sibling of B.

Every node keeps B after the heal. 3 slots is exactly the Lean formalization's bound for this phase (the outage plus its offset within the slot is at most (4k−1)Δ = 15Δ).

21 outage of 3.75 slots, B reverted.about:
The run of tab 20 with an outage of 3.75 slots, [t47+Δ, t51), beyond the Lean bound. After the heal C wins: every node drops B at t51+2Δ, after showing it for 36 s, and B is orphaned.

So the bound of the Lean proof is tight: the real tolerance is between 3 and 3.75 slots, depending on where the outage starts in the slot. The live spec's locks expire at the start of a slot and live Δ less, so its bound is Δ smaller.
